basis: Common respiratory, circulatory and renal failure; coagulation dysfunction often exceeds 30%. Hepatic and neurologic dysfunction omitted by cap; the organ combination varies.
Definition and children establish developmental eye disease; contradictory carcinoma and renal ancestry does not establish involvement.
Atrial septal defects define cardiac involvement. Congenital lymphedema and facial differences do not establish another damaged organ axis.
Inherited hepatic bilirubin transport disorder; normal liver histology. Jaundice and bilirubinuria do not establish skin, eye or kidney damage.
Red-cell membrane disorder; most patients are asymptomatic. Skin ulcers and gallstones are minority manifestations.
Inherited cardiomyopathy with ventricular structural and functional abnormalities; no established common extracardiac injury.
Immune-complex vasculitis with defining purpura and frequent skin ulcers; neuropathy 30-79%. Renal, GI and joint damage also frequent in supplied HPO, omitted by cap.
Inherited thyroid hormone synthesis defect. Intellectual disability lacks evidence of frequency sufficient for additional neurologic involvement.
Inherited retinal degeneration causing night blindness and visual impairment; optic atrophy remains within the ocular axis.
Noninvasive epithelial neoplasia confined to small-intestinal mucosa.
Hamartomatous polyps arise in the stomach or intestines; associated syndromes do not establish other involvement for this lesion.
Defining skeletal dysplasia and splenic hypo/aplasia; hypocalcemia in 5/5 supports metabolic involvement; hydrocephalus in 2/5 supports neurologic involvement.
Inherited serine biosynthesis disorder; developmental impairment, microcephaly and seizures affect most clinically affected patients.
Defining brain, kidney and optic nerve malformations; alopecia 80-99%. Skeletal, hearing and GI abnormalities at 30-79% omitted by cap.
Developmental delay, brachycephaly and trichomegaly define the syndrome; cleft palate and supernumerary tooth each reported in 1/2 support GI involvement. No anemia.
Mesenchymal tumor arising in connective and soft tissues around vessels; perivascular growth alone does not establish vascular dysfunction or a specific visceral origin.
Orbital bony margin agenesis and developmental abnormalities of eyelids and lacrimal drainage define the disorder.
Mutilating palmoplantar keratoderma; cheilitis in 4/4 supports oral involvement; fixed digital flexion contracture reported in 1/1 supports musculoskeletal involvement.
Inherited monoamine metabolism disorder with defining intellectual impairment; cognitive impairment occurs in 80-99%, so this is not purely psychiatric.
Epilepsy defined by an established metabolic etiology; both seizure disorder and metabolic abnormality characterize this group.
Isolated inherited displacement of the ocular lens; no systemic involvement is established.
Nonsyndromic progressive high-frequency hearing loss.
Immune-mediated inflammation of lung parenchyma following inhalation of domestic antigens.
Congenital aneurysmal dilatation of the ductus arteriosus. Airway compression, erosion and infection are possible complications without established frequency above 30%.
Inherited intracranial arterial aneurysm; cerebral injury from rupture is a complication, not established common direct brain involvement.
